claims.text: Alloying a pure transition-metal catalyst with a second metal can downshift the catalyst's d-band center.
A downshifted d-band center alters the adsorption strength of oxygenated intermediates.
The alloying modification will enhance catalytic selectivity under otherwise identical reaction conditions.
The energy position of the metal d-band center is the structural or electronic mediator modified by alloying.
Downshifting the d-band center reduces the binding strength of key oxygenated intermediates.
Reduced intermediate binding produces a more optimal adsorption-desorption balance.
The altered adsorption-desorption balance preferentially favors the desired pathway over side reactions.
The alloyed catalyst will have higher product selectivity than the pure-metal baseline.
Alloying may cause a slight change in overall catalytic activity.
The alloyed catalyst will exhibit a spectroscopically observable downshift of its d-band center relative to the pure-metal baseline.
The alloyed catalyst will exhibit altered adsorption energies of oxygenated intermediates relative to the pure-metal baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies when adsorption strength of oxygenated intermediates governs reaction selectivity.
Oxygen reduction and oxygen evolution are examples of reactions within the proposed mechanistic scope.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold at moderate temperatures below approximately 300 degrees Celsius where the electronic structure remains stable.
Morphological changes caused by alloying could influence catalytic behavior.
Catalyst-support effects could influence catalytic behavior.
XPS or UPS can be used to assess the d-band-center position.
In situ infrared spectroscopy can probe changes associated with intermediate adsorption.
